name: Alpha midline sine at IAF (sTMS timing)
origin: NeoSync synchronized TMS (sTMS): Leuchter, Cook et al. (UCLA and a multisite trial); the 3-coil mapping is a project construct
summary: Copies the timing of NeoSync's synchronized TMS (sTMS): a sine at the individual alpha frequency (10 Hz by default) for 30 min over three midline sites, Fpz, Fz and Cz, with neighbouring coils in antiphase. The device's rotating magnets had 0.64 T at their surface; this helmet's coils reach at most 0.48 mT at their face, over 1,000 times less. Only the timing is copied, not the tested device.
notes: sTMS spun 'three diametrically magnetized cylindrical neodymium magnets, 1-inch in diameter and length, with a surface field of 0.64 T' (Leuchter 2015 p.3) at the person's individual alpha frequency (IAF, 8 to 13 Hz, from a brief eyes-closed EEG) for 30 min. People lay still and relaxed, eyes closed and awake (NCT03288714 protocol p.25). The protocol's Figure 2 (p.25) draws the middle magnet with its poles reversed relative to the other two; the labels are small. This program reads that as neighbours in antiphase: Fpz and Cz play a 10 Hz sine, Fz an inverted copy (a 200-point table locked to the same 10 Hz). Fpz, Fz and Cz are this project's mapping of the magnet positions. A rotating magnet turns its field direction, while each coil only pulses along its own axis, so only the frequency, sites, duration and phase relation are copied. To use your own IAF, take N = 2000 / IAF rounded to a whole number, set f0 of track 1 to 2000 / N Hz and replace the table with N points of round(128-127*sin(2*pi*i/N)) at 0.5 ms. The magnets had 0.64 T at their surface; neither source gives the field at the scalp or cortex (Leuchter 2015 p.3; protocol p.24). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At the coil face the helmet gives 0.28 mT at this setting and 0.48 mT at its maximum, 1,300 to 2,300 times less than the magnet surface. There is one trial, funded by the sponsor: sTMS did not beat sham by intention to treat (n = 202) and did so only per protocol (n = 120) (Leuchter 2015 p.1-2). Cook 2019 reports midline alpha changes that tracked improvement on active treatment only. This program is not a treatment for depression or anything else; anyone with depression should see a clinician. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on discomfort.
setting: Lying face-up, still and relaxed, with eyes closed and awake, as in the trial (NCT03288714 protocol p.25), in a quiet room. The trial measured the IAF from a brief resting eyes-closed EEG before treatment; without one, keep the 10 Hz default.
schedule: Trial schedule: one 30-min session a day, 5 days a week for 6 weeks (30 sessions); the device locked out for 10 h after each session.
source: Leuchter et al. 2015, Brain Stimul https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26143022/ ; NCT03288714 study protocol (device, magnet sites, 30-min sessions, 10-h lockout) https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/14/NCT03288714/Prot_000.pdf ; Cook et al. 2019, Neuromodulation https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30637862/ ; Jin & Phillips 2014, sTMS pilot study (magnets rotate 180 degrees out of phase)

phases.name: IAF sine (10 Hz), Fz in antiphase
